account:
Today I have followed my appointments: office correspondence, the market walk, lunch at home, and an attempted review of town accounts. I have now reached the east-bank dockside cottage for tea at three; neighbour is waiting by the open door. The secretary confirmed this invitation personally and filed its confirmation in the appointments chest. I do not yet know what neighbour wants to discuss or whether this is more than an ordinary social visit.

I have a feeling something may be happening without my knowledge, but have found no confirmed evidence of a secret gathering or other unusual undertaking. Several townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery. The baker said they stocked thirty-two fresh loaves, reported no difficulties or confirmed news, and asked whether upcoming town gatherings would need bread. This could simply be ordinary business and an attempt to obtain advance orders; I know of no gathering to connect it to.

The town accounts remain unresolved. The treasury contains 128 emeralds but no account books. The secretary reports no new correspondence, reported outstanding payments, unusual expenses, or funding requests, but has not examined the accounts and does not know where the records are. That is a gap in our knowledge, not proof of missing funds or misconduct. My last reply about locating records was not heard, so I cannot assume the secretary received those instructions. Tea may give me an opportunity to learn more local news before my scheduled return to the office at half past four.
